literal_source_claim: A family of finite character has a maximal element.
canonical_claim: For every type alpha and family F of subsets of alpha, if F is nonempty and has finite character (X belongs to F exactly when every finite subset of X belongs to F), then F contains an inclusion-maximal member. Equivalently in the pointed form: every x in F is contained in some inclusion-maximal m in F.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: forall {alpha : Type u} {F : Set (Set alpha)}, Order.IsOfFiniteCharacter F -> forall {x : Set alpha}, x in F -> exists m, x subseteq m and Maximal (fun y => y in F) m

domain_and_universes: An arbitrary universe u, a type alpha : Type u, and a family F : Set (Set alpha), ordered by subset inclusion.

seed x : Set alpha in the pointed form
hypotheses: F has finite character: for every X, X is in F iff every finite subset of X is in F
F is nonempty; represented in the candidate pointed form by a witness x in F
conclusion: There exists m in F maximal under inclusion; in the pointed form x is a subset of m and m is maximal among members of F.

excluded_degenerate_cases: The empty family is excluded because it has finite character vacuously under the standard biconditional definition but has no maximal member. Maximal means maximal among members of F under subset inclusion, not a greatest member and not a maximal set in the entire powerset. Alpha may be empty and family members may be empty; these are not excluded.
